topline.text: Sheffield's finance committee approved extra funding for a new SEND facility at Stocksbridge Junior School — total budget now £823,000.
topline.action: Worth logging alongside Monday's exclusions discussion.

topline.text: NAHT is calling for graded Ofsted inspections to be halted, warning the framework poses 'a real and present danger' to leader wellbeing.
Schools Week disputes DfE's claim the 2026-27 teacher pay award is 'fully funded'; NEU's executive responds on 24 September.
A quieter day otherwise — nothing else new broke overnight across DfE, SEND or national funding beyond what's already on your radar.

diary.text: NEU's national executive decides its formal response to the 2026-27 pay award, after Schools Week challenged DfE's 'fully funded' claim.
NEU opens a formal strike ballot over teacher pay and school funding, covering 280,000+ teachers; closes 15 Dec.

items.lede: Sheffield approves extra £758k for new SEND facility at Stocksbridge Junior School.
items.body: The finance and performance policy committee backed additional funding on Monday, taking the total to £823,000, for a Key Stage 2 Integrated Resource Provision for pupils with communication and interaction needs — citing rising local demand and families travelling long distances. Due to complete by May 2027; figures as reported ahead of published committee papers.
items.action: A local capacity signal worth logging alongside Monday's exclusions discussion.

items.lede: NAHT calls for graded Ofsted inspections to be halted, citing risk to leader wellbeing.
items.body: A survey of 5,000+ school leaders found nearly three-quarters feel inspection has worsened over the past year, one year on from the report-card reforms. General secretary Paul Whiteman said the framework poses 'a real and present danger' to leaders' wellbeing; the union wants grades replaced with a short narrative report pending a review.
items.action: Worth watching how this lands with leaders you support — inspection stress can ripple into inclusion decisions.

items.lede: Is the 'fully funded' teacher pay rise actually new money? Schools Week says no.
items.body: DfE says the 3.5% pay award is fully funded via ~£500m/year in pension savings, but Schools Week argues schools already budgeted for those lower rates from April — so there's no genuine new money, and the saving varies school to school.
items.action: Useful if finance leads ask why 'fully funded' doesn't match their budget reality.

box.text: Total budget approved by Sheffield's finance and performance policy committee for a new SEND Integrated Resource Provision at Stocksbridge Junior School, due to open by May 2027.
